body:
Primary-source leads for architecture slides:
- PPTX: python-pptx exposes immutable-within-deck `slide_id`, shapes, and notes-slide APIs; useful for stable IDs + extraction: https://python-pptx.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/slides.html . LibreOffice supports `--headless` and `--convert-to`; use conversion/rendering for fidelity, not python-pptx alone: https://help.libreoffice.org/latest/en-US/text/shared/guide/start_parameters.html . PDF text blocks/words carry position metadata in PyMuPDF: https://pymupdf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/recipes-text.html . Reveal.js emits immediate `slidechanged`: https://revealjs.com/events/ .
- Korean STT candidates: Azure docs explicitly list `ko-KR`, intermediate Recognizing results and final Recognized results, plus utterance/word timing: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/language-support?tabs=stt and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/get-speech-recognition-results . Google V2 defines interim vs final plus stability and resultEndOffset: https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/v2/docs/reference/rest/v2/StreamingRecognitionResult . AWS explicitly lists Korean batch+streaming and partial stabilization latency/accuracy tradeoff: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/supported-languages.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming-partial-results.html . Deepgram Nova-3 lists Korean and documents interim/final + configurable endpointing (300-500 ms suggested for conversational pauses): https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/models-languages-overview and https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/understand-endpointing-interim-results . Vendor docs prove semantics/support, NOT Korean WER or observed latency—benchmark on target microphones/code-switch speech.
- Event transport: Redis Streams consumer groups require explicit XACK and retain pending work: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/xreadgroup/ . NATS JetStream is at-least-once and redelivers unacked events: https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream . MVP favors Redis Streams if Redis already needed for sessions/cooldowns; NATS only when multiple independently deployed consumers/scale justify another service. Consumers must be idempotent.
- Hybrid/ACL: Azure runs vector+full-text in parallel then RRF and supports prefilter: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/hybrid-search-overview and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/vector-search-filters . CRITICAL caveat: Azure's documented security-filter pattern says the principal is 'just a string' and is not authentication/authorization; app must authenticate and derive principals server-side: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-trimming-for-azure-search . PostgreSQL RLS is stronger/default-deny and evaluates policy before query conditions: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html . For MVP, Postgres+pgvector+FTS+RLS is the smallest safe stack; pgvector docs endorse FTS hybrid/RRF but warn ANN filtering occurs after scan unless tuned/iterative scans: https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector .
- External search: Brave offers freshness/language filters but snippets are previews, not evidence: https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/app/documentation/web-search/get-started . Tavily exposes ultra-fast search and optional raw cleaned content, but original fetch/anchor verification still required: https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search .
summary: Primary-source stack evidence and a critical ACL caveat
